title: Ophir Co Limited - Monthly Exploration Report June 2026
content: Monthly Exploration Report for June 2026. Company: Ophir Company Ltd. Author: Sampson Nsiah, B.Sc. Reviewed by: Collins Asseto, B.Sc Nbi; M.S. Auburn.

title: June 2026 Sampling and Assaying Progress
content: Mapping of Eastern Block 1 ongoing. Mapping of Artisanal workings ongoing. 135 grab samples collected, 45 sent to lab for analysis. 45 samples results pending. Total 145 samples collected from May and June. 76 collected in June. 45 sent to lab, waiting for results. 100 samples ready for dispatch in camp (channel/grab from artisanal mining stream bank).

title: June 2026 Sample Dispatch Plan
content: Sample Dispatch Plan: Week 1: 70 samples x $20 = $1,400. Week 2: 70 samples x $20 = $1,400. Week 3: 70 samples x $20 = $1,400. Total: 210 samples, Total cost: $4,200.

title: June 2026 GPS/UTM Sample Locations - Block 1 (Eastern Shear Zone)
content: Block 1 located on eastern Shear Zone. ~3.50km from camp site to Ophir Processing Plant. Block 1 mapping began: 5th June 2026, completed: 31st July 2026. Emphasis: NE-SW trending structures, E-W trending structures, artisanal workings, outcrops, road cuts, alluvial working areas. Grid lines generated across interpreted regional shear structures. Areas around Koyokonyo - surface exposures observed. Active/abandoned artisanal mining pits near Koyonkoyo stream. Main lithologies: granitic gneiss, schistose gneiss, Quartz feldspar-pegmatite, Biotite gneiss, mafic rocks, floats of quartz porphyry, brecciated (sheared) quartz vein. 45 channel/grab samples taken, submitted to SGS laboratory in Mwanza. Structural dips: steep average 73 degrees, adjacent quartz vein moderately dipping 60 degrees.

content: Block 1 located on eastern Shear Zone. ~3.50km from camp site to Ophir Processing Plant. Mapping began 5th June 2026, completed 31st July 2026. NE-SW trending structures, E-W trending structures. Artisanal workings, outcrops, road cuts, alluvial working areas. Grid lines across regional shear structures. Areas around Koyokonyo - surface exposures observed. Active/abandoned artisanal mining pits near Koyonkoyo stream. Main lithologies: granitic gneiss, schistose gneiss, Quartz feldspar-pegmatite, Biotite gneiss, mafic rocks, floats of quartz porphyry, brecciated (sheared) quartz vein. 45 channel/grab samples taken, submitted to SGS laboratory in Mwanza. Structural dips: steep average 73 degrees, adjacent quartz vein moderately dipping 60 degrees.

title: June 2026 Field Photos - Artisanal Mining and Quartz Veins
content: Figure 2: Active artisanal mining area showing granitic gneiss and highly brecciated quartz veins (steep and moderate dips). Figure 3: Artisanal mining workings near Koyokonyo. Figure 4: Massive body of Quartz-feldspar peg with evidence of fluid movement. Au seen in hand specimen. Fe-oxide rich QV (sheared zone). Ferruginous/laterite. Mottled saprolite. Oxide materials (Fe/Al oxides). Figure 4 (second): Overturned to isoclinal fold in Artisanal workings stream. Strike = 324 degrees. Structural traps and stress fractures creating pathways for ore-bearing hydrothermal fluids. Figure 5: Overturned to isoclinal fold at bank of Artisanal workings stream. Figure 6: Weathered quartz-feldspar-pegmatite intruding metamorphic rock (gneiss). Iron stained fractures/shear zone.

title: June 2026 Laiya Basin and Placer Target
content: Figure 7: Laiya basin - loose unconsolidated material, large number of women artisanal miners. Figure 8: Potential placer deposit, locally constructed gold trap site.

title: June 2026 Field Observations
content: NE and Eastern artisanal mining: strong chloritic-epidote, Fe-oxide, K-feldspars, hematite alteration. Sub-vertical quartz vein stringers. Strong ch-epidote, limonite alteration with shear zones. Strike = 324 degrees.

title: June 2026 Forward Plans for July 2026
content: Forward Plans: 1. Send outstanding samples to lab. 2. Review high resolution satellite data. 3. Trench a target vein in artisanal working area. 4. Mapping, sampling, backfilling trenching within artisanal workings. 5. Continue extensive mapping/sampling at Eastern Block 1. 6. 3 trenches in targeted areas to understand subsurface geology and primary Au source. 7. Continue field mapping.
